differences.title: 1. ROLE IN THE PIPELINE
differences.leftDesc: OpenTelemetry defines a vendor-neutral model (spans, metrics, logs) plus SDKs and collectors. It standardizes how apps emit telemetry so multiple backends can consume the same data format.
differences.rightDesc: Jaeger is a distributed tracing backend that primarily focuses on storing and rendering traces. It ingests span data, indexes it for fast lookup, and provides trace views and search-centric UX for debugging.

differences.title: 2. DATA MODEL COVERAGE
differences.leftDesc: OpenTelemetry supports traces, metrics, and (optionally) logs via its APIs. The same SDK can create spans and metric instruments, then export to an OpenTelemetry Collector pipeline.
differences.rightDesc: Jaeger is optimized around tracing semantics: span timelines, parent-child relationships, and trace graphs. Metrics/logs are not its primary abstraction; it expects span streams for analysis.

differences.title: 3. TRANSPORT & INGESTION
differences.leftDesc: Most OpenTelemetry deployments export using OTLP (gRPC or HTTP) from SDKs/agents to an OpenTelemetry Collector. The Collector handles batching, retries, and routing to multiple exporters.
differences.rightDesc: Jaeger typically receives spans via its collector/ingestion endpoints (often through the OpenTelemetry Collector using a Jaeger exporter). Jaeger’s ingestion converts span payloads into internal storage records.

differences.title: 4. SAMPLING & VOLUME CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: OpenTelemetry can apply sampling at the SDK and collector layers using configurable samplers. You can combine head-based and tail-based approaches to reduce overhead while preserving important traces.
differences.rightDesc: Jaeger commonly uses tail-based sampling strategies when integrated with sampling plugins/collectors. It can keep high-value spans based on latency/errors, trading memory/throughput for fidelity.

differences.title: 5. STORAGE & QUERY PATH
differences.leftDesc: OpenTelemetry does not dictate long-term storage. It exports telemetry to whichever backend you configure (e.g., Jaeger, Tempo, vendor platforms). Query semantics come from the destination.
differences.rightDesc: Jaeger manages trace storage and lookup indexes internally or via storage backends (such as Elasticsearch). It’s designed for fast retrieval of trace trees, searchable by service/operation and time range.

differences.title: 6. ECS/SEMANTIC CONSISTENCY
differences.leftDesc: OpenTelemetry encourages consistent attribute naming through Semantic Conventions (e.g., HTTP method/route, DB system). Instrumentations map runtime concepts into standardized span/metric attributes.
differences.rightDesc: Jaeger expects span attributes but primarily focuses on how traces are visualized and navigated. It relies on instrumentation to provide meaningful tags; normalization is less about standards.

differences.title: 7. OPERATIONS & SCALING MODEL
differences.leftDesc: OpenTelemetry scales horizontally by running SDKs/agents across services and a shared OpenTelemetry Collector fleet. Pipelines can buffer, transform, and fan-out exports with backpressure controls.
differences.rightDesc: Jaeger scales via its ingestion/agent components plus storage backends. Throughput depends on ingestion capacity and index/write performance; retention strategies heavily impact storage cost and query speed.
